text:
morgan_pm: quick sync — we need a concise GA acceptance checklist for the embedded / SDK customers. goal: a single page that legal/commercial/ops can point to when they onboard. low-friction, must cover SLA, pricing footguns, docs, support training, and observability handoffs.

alex_eng: can you list the non-negotiables you want on the page?

morgan_pm: non-negotiables: 1) SLA tiers & response targets (p1/p2) 2) required docs & example flows (init, token rotation, error handling) 3) oncall + escalation path + runbook links 4) monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds 5) pricing guardrails (burst limits, quota/overage behavior) 6) rollout plan for customers that need private/dedicated.

jia_sre: + note: we should include fallbacks (model variant fallback) and expected latency bands per tier. also note typical warmup time for dedicated pools.

sofia_support: love that. for support readiness: need playbook snippets for the top 5 customer issues during first 2 weeks (auth, degraded throughput, billing disputes, model regressions, infra errors). can we put owners next to each?

morgan_pm: yes — owners column. suggested owners: auth -> eng-platform, throughput -> runtime team, billing -> finance ops, model regressions -> applied-ml + product, infra errors -> eng-sre.

tariq_finops: pricing guardrails: must call out when cost-based throttling kicks in and what the customer sees in console + notification cadence. also clarify how credits, reserved capacity, and meter-based billing interplay.

alex_eng: on the SLA numbers: propose SLOs for GA: 99.9% availability for hosted, 99.95% for dedicated (subject to infra), p1 response within 1 hour, p2 within 4 hours. are those acceptable?

morgan_pm: those are fine as starting points. add an explicit exception list (third-party infra outage, customer network issues) and a clear mitigation policy for persistent violations.

jia_sre: monitoring: we'll publish dashboards for token-level latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), error rate, queue length, and GPU utilization. alerts: error-rate > 0.5% sustained 5m -> page, p99 latency > X ms -> page for dedicated. I'll add exact thresholds in doc.

sofia_support: training: need a 60-minute enablement + playbook walk-through recorded and a short FAQ for customers. also internal runbook with troubleshooting checklist and sample `curl` repro cases.

morgan_pm: documentation owners: alex -> runtime + SDK quickstart, jia -> observability & runbooks, sofia -> support playbook + FAQ, tariq -> billing & pricing page.

alex_eng: for SDK quickstart, I'll add a minimal embedded flow showing offline token refresh and exponential backoff snippet:`
```
// pseudo
client = RedwoodSDK({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY})
res = await client.generate({model: 'redwood-2', prompt: 'hi'})
```

morgan_pm: also include a short section on what to do for large batch/throughput customers — recommended batching config, KV cache hints, and quantization compatibility notes.

jia_sre: rollout plan: staged canary by customer size + fallback lanes. propose: 1) internal beta (2 customers) 2) small customers (<=1M tokens/day) 3) mid (1–50M) with finance-approved terms 4) large enterprise on Dedicated with reserved capacity. each stage requires sign-off on SLAs, billing terms, and runbook readiness.

tariq_finops: add finance gating: for stages 3-4 we need a billing review and an approved quota/commit schedule. also pre-announce overage behavior and required PO/contract changes.

sofia_support: how do we handle customers who want custom SLAs? template: standard GA SLA + addendum template for legal to review. we should include an example clause for incident credits and remedies.

morgan_pm: yes — include sample addendum + process: customer asks -> AM -> legal -> finance -> SLA executed. timeline note: typical negotiation 2–4 weeks.

alex_eng: operationally, we need explicit compatibility matrix in docs: SDK version X -> runtime version Y -> supported model quantization. prevents support churn.

jia_sre: and a short troubleshooting cheat-sheet: 'isolate source of failure' steps: 1) curl minimal repro 2) check token billing vs quota 3) check region routing/fallback 4) escalate with perf trace link.

rollout-bot: reminder: draft checklist doc created at https://docs.internal/redwood/ga-acceptance-draft (auto).

morgan_pm: next steps: alex + jia + sofia + tariq each drop a one-paragraph section by EOD Wed. I'll consolidate and run a 30-min shiproom Thu for signoffs. please call out any red flags now.

sofia_support: red flag: we need an SLA-compatible support staffing plan for the first 90 days (weekend coverage for P1s). don't want to promise 24/7 without ops staffing.

jia_sre: agrees — we will provide oncall coverage but need a written commit window for weekend escalation for GA customers.

tariq_finops: red flag: reserved capacity up-front pricing approval may delay some enterprise deals. propose a 'trial commit' option for 30 days with soft upper cap.

alex_eng: technical red flag: dedicated warm pool time for some models = ~10–15 minutes on cold start. document behavior and suggested pre-warm procedures for customers.

morgan_pm: great points. I'll add these as 'deal-breaker' notes in the doc. thanks team — please post your short paragraphs to the draft link and I'll merge. :thumbsup:
